svg.title: Choosing a data centre interconnect technology: four scenarios mapped to VPLS, EVPN or PBB-EVPN
svg.desc: Four scenario rows. Few data centres with few interconnect points map to VPLS because it is simple and mature. Many data centres with many interconnect points map to EVPN or PBB-EVPN for scalability. A strong MAC mobility requirement maps to EVPN because MACs are advertised in the control plane. An enormous number of MAC addresses maps to PBB-EVPN because it hides customer MACs. A note at the bottom says the order of the questions matters: first ask whether Layer 2 extension is needed at all, then count the MACs, and only then name a technology.
svg.text: DCI is not a technology question first — it is a count of sites, links and MAC addresses
The same three protocols, read as four answers to four different measurements
two or three sites, one path each
team already knows it, and the mesh is small
the mesh no longer fits in a spreadsheet
High scalability: routes replace the mesh,
and new sites are added without touching peers
and users notice every second of it
MAC advertisement in the control plane,
so movement is a route update, not a flood
MAC hiding: the core carries B-MACs only,
customer churn stops at the BEB
Ask the questions in this order, or the answer will be wrong: does this workload actually need one Layer 2 domain across the two sites?
If it does not, a Layer 3 DCI removes this table entirely. If it does, count the MACs and the sites before naming a protocol — the protocol is the last decision, not the first.
Scenario 1 at the end of this chapter is exactly this question, with a manager who has already decided the answer.
